routines.semantics: Return the zero-based index of the last character array element less than or equal to the key, or −1 for empty input or no qualifying element. Nondecreasing order is a caller precondition. Preserve supplied order and duplicates. Well-formed UTF-8 keys/rows reject embedded NUL. Compare unsigned bytes under ASCII blank extension, with equivalent trailing spaces. Each rectangular row has width max(2,longest encoded row+1), blank-filled through its character area and terminated by NUL in the last byte. Key and table fit signed 32-bit byte counts.

scenarios.observes: Pass an inferred count of zero using actual valid storage and compare exact −1 at several keys.
Query below, equal to and above the single entry. Distinguish −1 from valid index zero.
Search repeated values at multiple positions, retaining the exact index of the last qualifying entry for equal and surrounding queries.
Use rows differing only by trailing ASCII spaces. Observe rightmost inclusive equality and strict predecessor behavior.
Use empty/blank keys and rows under blank extension and compare exact index results.
Use a tab byte smaller than ASCII space, including an interior row. The fixture discriminates space-padded rows from early-NUL or zero-padded representations.
Distinguish byte order of punctuation, digits, uppercase and lowercase ASCII entries without locale collation or case folding.
Observe sorted unsigned UTF-8 order including multi-byte and supplementary characters whose JS UTF-16 order differs.
Compare longer keys with rows that are common prefixes, retaining blank-extension comparison and exact index.

routines.edgeAssessment: Empty arrays, singleton keys and duplicate runs at each end and internally compare exact −1 and index zero through the highest qualifying index. All-equal trailing blanks, empty strings/blank keys, controls, punctuation, case, unsigned UTF-8 ordering and long common prefixes distinguish the fixed-width representation.
routines.errorAssessment: No scientific error is fabricated for valid sorted inputs, and an empty array genuinely returns −1. Unsorted input violates the documented caller precondition. Test-side validation rejects unsorted fixtures before independent calls. Malformed types and unsafe count/byte sizes are separate wrapper checks.
routines.fixtureRationale: Project-authored sorted arrays and keys with discriminating duplicate/control-byte/ordering cases. No kernel or dataset resources.
routines.cleanup: Capture array lengths, copy validated entries once and check storage before calls. Native owns storage during serialized calls. WASM uses transactional allocations and reads the scalar only after successful status. Valid non-null dummy storage supports zero count. Focused public clients dispose cleanly.
routines.tolerance: Compare exact integer indices, including −1. No tolerance is meaningful for an index. Public comparisons also distinguish adjacent doubles and correctly padded byte rows using independently observed integral outputs.

findings.summary: The pinned inclusive character routine compares endpoints with strlen but compares an interior row with arrlen−1 bytes. Ordinary zero-filled rectangular row padding can alter the ordering against a low control byte.
findings.repair: Both adapters and the independent SpiceyPy caller encode the same fixed-width row, pad with ASCII spaces and add the terminating NUL in its last byte. The probe inspects exact bytes and runs both canonical inclusive and strict calls with ordinary and space-filled rows.

findings.summary: The native test matcher inspected an instrumented input after dispatch, affecting the test read count.
findings.repair: Use Object.is for identity and pass only its boolean result to the matcher. This keeps the native delegation ownership assertion observable.
